questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code validates and sanitizes user-supplied input? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A rider submits pickup_note = "Gate B". What is stored in rides.note?
choices: The request is rejected with 422 because it contains markup.
Gate B, because bleach.clean with no allowed tags and strip=True drops the tags and keeps the text.
<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>Gate B, because bleach always escapes disallowed tags.
The original string, because the validator only runs for strings longer than 280 characters.

questions.prompt: ride_history builds its ORDER BY clause with an f-string. Why is that acceptable here, and why not use a bound parameter for it?
choices: It is acceptable because SQLAlchemy's text() escapes interpolated values automatically.
It is acceptable because the limit is capped at 200 rows.
The column name comes from a fixed allow-list (SORT_COLUMNS), and identifiers cannot be bound as parameters, so only known values are ever interpolated.
It is not acceptable; bound parameters work for column names too.

questions.prompt: A request asks for GET /v1/receipts//etc/passwd, so name = "/etc/passwd". What does receipt_path return?
choices: None, because RECEIPT_DIR / "/etc/passwd" yields /etc/passwd (an absolute right operand replaces the base), which is not inside RECEIPT_DIR.
The contents of /etc/passwd, because resolve() follows the absolute path.
None, but only because /etc/passwd is not a file.
